context: Kickoff notes. Client: Bright Smile Clinic. Contacts: Dr. Nina Hale (owner), Sara (office manager). Project: a new website with online booking. Scope: 5 pages, booking form connected to the CalDesk calendar, no mobile app. Timeline: 8 weeks. Budget: $18,000. Client sends content by the end of week 2. Changes after design approval need a change request. Dan is the project manager.

lines.text: Welcome everyone, and thank you for joining the kickoff. Nina, Sara, great to see you.

lines.speaker: Nina
lines.text: Thank you Dan. We are excited. Sara will be involved in the daily details.
Let us start with roles. I will be your project manager for the whole project.

lines.speaker: Nina
lines.text: Good. Who is our contact on your side if you are on vacation?
I will name a backup before I take any time off.

lines.speaker: Sara
lines.text: Let me ask about scope. I thought we have ten pages, not five.
Our scope document says five pages. We can discuss more as a change.

lines.speaker: Nina
lines.text: Okay. And what happens if we want to change something after we approve the design?
After approval, changes go through a change request so we can check the effect.

lines.speaker: Nina
lines.text: Fine. We would also like a mobile app for patients, can we add it?
The mobile app is not in this scope. We can plan it as a second phase.

lines.speaker: Sara
lines.text: What is the budget again? I have it as twenty five thousand.
The agreed budget is $18,000 for this scope.

lines.speaker: Nina
lines.text: OK. Eight weeks feels long to me. A competitor told us five weeks.
What did they include in those five weeks?

lines.speaker: Nina
lines.text: Not sure. We can ask them.

lines.speaker: Sara
lines.text: Nina, did you call the photographer about the clinic photos?

lines.speaker: Nina
lines.text: Not yet, I will do it tomorrow.
We will also need the clinic photos and texts. We call that content, and it comes from you.

lines.speaker: Sara
lines.text: We will send everything by the end of next week, I promise.
Great. That is week two in the plan, which is what we need. Then I will send you a kickoff summary today.

lines.speaker: Nina
lines.text: Who signs off on the design on our side? I do, or should Sara do it?
Let me come back to that when we reach the design stage.

lines.speaker: Sara
lines.text: Another thing. The CalDesk system sometimes responds slowly. Will that affect the booking?
Good point, we will add it to the risk list.

lines.speaker: Nina
lines.text: Also, do we get a staging site where we can test before launch? What is that exactly?
Yes, a private test copy of the site, before launch.

lines.speaker: Sara
lines.text: And then the UAT before the launch, I read about that.
Right, your team checks the site and confirms it works for you.

lines.speaker: Nina
lines.text: How often will we meet during the project?
A weekly status call. I will send a proposal for the time.

lines.speaker: Nina
lines.text: By the way, we had a hard month with staff. Two hygienists left.
Sorry to hear that. Let us make sure the booking helps your team, then. Back to the plan.

lines.speaker: Sara
lines.text: Dan, can you send me the contract copy again?
Sure, I will send it after the call.
To close, I still need to know who signs off on the design.

lines.speaker: Nina
lines.text: Sara will approve the design, and I will approve the final launch.
Perfect. Thank you both.

lines.speaker: Nina
lines.text: Thank you Dan.
